An email account intended to send large numbers of messages, which can be abused to distribute spam or phishing emails.
Bundled confirmation technique
A single approval prompt that asks a user to authorize several actions at once.
also: multiple approvals
Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives organization
A U.S. federal law-enforcement agency commonly known as the ATF.
Bypass technique
A bypass is a way to get around a security check, restriction, or protection.
Bypass authentication technique
Bypass authentication means getting into a system without passing the normal login checks.
cache concept
A cache is a temporary storage area that keeps frequently used data so it can be loaded faster later.
California other
California is a U.S. state often referenced in technology, privacy, and cybersecurity policy.
canada
Canada is a North American country often referenced in cybersecurity reporting as a target, regulator, or law-enforcement partner.
also: Canadian
Capability concept
A capability is something a person, tool, system, or attacker is able to do.
CAPTCHA concept
A test that tells humans and computers apart, often by asking you to click on pictures or type distorted letters.
CAPTCHA gating technique
A technique that requires visitors to complete a CAPTCHA before they can reach a website or its content.
capture concept
A capture is a part of a regular expression that saves matched text so it can be reused or referenced later.
cash-out contractors concept
People who receive and convert illegally obtained funds into cash or other usable forms for criminals.
CDN concept
A CDN, or content delivery network, is a group of servers that helps deliver websites and files faster by serving them from locations closer to users.
also: CDNs, content-delivery edge
CDN edge concept
A CDN edge is a server near users that delivers cached website content on behalf of a content delivery network.
CenQL tool
CenQL is Censys’s query language for searching and filtering internet asset data.
CensEye tool
A Censys tool for finding related internet-connected systems by comparing shared technical characteristics.
also: CensEye Pivots
Census Labs organization
Census Labs is a security research organization.
censys tool
Censys is an internet scanning and search platform used to discover exposed systems and certificates.
also: Censys Platform
Censys Active DNS product
Censys Active DNS is a Censys data product that actively queries DNS records to help map domains and internet infrastructure.
Censys ARC product
Censys ARC is a Censys product or service used for analyzing and monitoring internet-exposed assets and risks.
also: ARC
Censys ASM product
Censys ASM is an external attack surface management product that helps organizations discover and monitor their internet-exposed assets.
also: ASM
Censys Investigator product
Censys Investigator is a Censys product used by security teams to search and investigate internet-exposed systems and infrastructure.
also: Investigator
Center for Open Science organization
A nonprofit organization that operates research-sharing services including the Open Science Framework.
Certificate Authority concept
A trusted organization or service that issues and signs digital certificates.
also: CA, CAs, certificate authority (CA)
Certificate Data concept
Information in a digital certificate that helps a system verify an identity and establish encrypted communications.
certificate transparency concept
Certificate transparency is a system of public logs that lets people check which website certificates have been issued.
also: CT, CT logs, Certificate Transparency (CT) logs
Certified Pre-Owned other
A SpecterOps research publication describing ways attackers can abuse Microsoft Active Directory Certificate Services.
also: SpecterOps’ “Certified Pre-Owned” research
certutil tool
certutil is a Windows command-line tool for managing certificates that attackers sometimes abuse to download or decode files.
certutil.exe tool
certutil.exe is a legitimate Windows command-line tool for certificate tasks that attackers also abuse to download or encode files.
chaining multiple zero-days technique
Linking several previously unknown security flaws so that together they can achieve a larger compromise than any one flaw alone.
Chalk tool
Chalk is a JavaScript library commonly used by developers to add color and formatting to command-line text.
changelog concept
A changelog is a list of updates showing what changed between versions of software.
Chatbot instructions concept
Text intended to direct an AI chatbot’s behavior or responses.
chatgpt
ChatGPT is OpenAI’s conversational AI assistant.
Check Point organization
Check Point is a cybersecurity company known for firewall, network security, cloud security, and threat prevention products.
Checkmarx organization
Checkmarx is a cybersecurity company known for tools that scan software code for security vulnerabilities.
Checkmarx One product
Checkmarx One is an application security platform used to find vulnerabilities in software code and development pipelines.
china
China is a country often referenced in cybersecurity reporting involving technology, espionage, regulation, and threat activity.
China-linked concept
China-linked describes activity, groups, or infrastructure believed to have some connection to China.
Chinese company organization
A company based in China or associated with Chinese ownership or operations.
Chinese government organization
The Chinese government is the national government of China and is often referenced in security reporting about state-linked cyber activity.
choke points concept
Choke points are places in a system or process where blocking or controlling one part can greatly affect everything that depends on it.
CI/CD Secrets concept
Sensitive passwords, keys, or tokens used by automated software building and deployment systems.
cisa organization
CISA is the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, which helps protect critical infrastructure and shares security guidance.
CISA KEV concept
CISA KEV is the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency's catalog of known exploited vulnerabilities that defenders should prioritize fixing.
CISA Known Exploited Vulnerability concept
A designation for a software vulnerability that the U.S. cybersecurity agency CISA knows is being exploited in real attacks.
cisa-known-exploited-vulnerabilities organization
CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities is a U.S. government catalog of security flaws confirmed to be exploited by attackers.
Citrix organization
Citrix is a company known for remote access, virtualization, and application delivery products.
Citrix NetScaler product
Citrix NetScaler is a product line for application delivery, load balancing, and secure remote access, now commonly branded as NetScaler.
also: NetScaler appliances, candidate NetScaler appliances
Citrix NetScaler Zero-Days vulnerability
Previously unknown security flaws in Citrix NetScaler products that attackers may exploit before fixes are available.
Classified concept
Classified information is government information restricted because releasing it could harm national security or other protected interests.
claude
Claude is Anthropic’s family of AI assistants and language models.
Claude Models product
Claude is a family of artificial-intelligence language models made by Anthropic.
Claude Mythos product
Claude Mythos is a named AI-related product or model referenced in reporting.
claude-code
Claude Code is Anthropic’s AI coding assistant for helping developers write and manage software projects.
cleartext concept
Cleartext is data that is readable as-is because it is not encrypted.
click-tracking technique
Click-tracking is a way to record when someone clicks a link, often used in marketing emails and sometimes abused in phishing.
clickfix
ClickFix is a social-engineering tactic that tricks users into copying and running malicious commands to “fix” a fake problem.
also: ClickFix self-infection
Clinical systems concept
Clinical systems are healthcare technologies used to support patient care, records, scheduling, testing, or treatment.
clipboard concept
The clipboard is the temporary place where copied text, images, or files are stored before pasting.
Cloaking technique
A technique that shows different web content to different visitors, often hiding malicious pages from security checks.
cloud concept
The cloud is internet-based computing where data and applications run on remote servers instead of only on your own device.
Cloud accounts concept
Cloud accounts are identities or subscriptions used to access services hosted by providers like AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud.
Cloud Identities concept
User accounts, service accounts, and roles that can access resources in a cloud environment.
cloud identity abuse technique
The misuse of cloud user accounts, service accounts, or their permissions to gain unauthorized access to online systems.
Cloud Posture concept
Cloud posture is the overall security state of an organization's cloud services and settings.
cloud resources concept
Cloud resources are computing services like servers, storage, databases, or apps that run in an internet-hosted cloud environment.
Cloud security concept
Cloud security means protecting data, applications, and accounts that run in cloud services.
cloud services concept
Computing resources—like storage, apps, and networking—delivered over the internet by providers such as AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud.
cloud systems concept
Cloud systems are computer services and data storage run on internet-connected servers instead of only on a person's or company's own machines.
cloud workloads concept
Applications or services running on cloud infrastructure, such as virtual machines or containers.
cloudflare
Cloudflare is a company that provides content delivery, DDoS protection, DNS, and web security services.
Cloudflare Pages product
Cloudflare Pages is a Cloudflare service for hosting and deploying websites, especially static sites and frontend applications.
CloudFormation product
CloudFormation is an AWS service for defining and deploying cloud infrastructure using templates.
CloudTrail product
CloudTrail is an AWS service that records management API activity.
cluster concept
A group of connected computers or appliances that work together as one system.
co-conspirators threat-actor
Co-conspirators are people who work together with others to plan or commit a crime.
code change concept
A code change is an edit to software source code that can add features, fix bugs, or change behavior.
code execution technique
Code execution means an attacker can make a computer or server run commands or software of their choosing.
code of the attacker's choice technique
Program instructions selected by an attacker that they are able to make a target device run.
Code Quality concept
Code quality describes how reliable, readable, maintainable, and secure software code is.
code repository tool
A code repository is an online or local storage place where software source code and its change history are kept.
CodeQL tool
CodeQL is GitHub's code analysis tool that searches source code for bugs and security vulnerabilities.
also: GitHub’s semantic analysis engine
codex
Codex is an OpenAI AI coding model or coding assistant technology for helping write and understand code.
coding concept
Coding is writing instructions in a programming language so a computer can perform tasks.
Coding agents tool
Coding agents are AI tools that can help write, edit, test, or reason about software code.
command execution technique
Command execution means making a computer or device run instructions, often through a shell or remote interface.
command injection technique
Command injection is an attack where someone tricks an application into running system commands chosen by the attacker.
command-and-control (C2) concept
Command-and-control, or C2, is the attacker-controlled communication channel used to manage compromised computers.
also: C2
commit concept
A saved set of changes in a version-control system such as Git.
commits concept
Commits are saved sets of changes to files in a source-code repository.
Complete control concept
Complete control means an attacker can fully manage a system, account, or application as if they owned it.
Composite authentication concept
Composite authentication is using several identity or message-checking signals together to decide whether something is trustworthy.
compromise concept
A compromise is a situation where a system, account, or data has been breached or taken over by an attacker.
compromised concept
Compromised means a system, account, or device has been accessed or controlled by someone who should not have access.
compromised accounts concept
Compromised accounts are user accounts that attackers have gained access to without permission.
Compromised devices concept
Compromised devices are computers, phones, or systems that attackers have gained unauthorized control over.
Compromised hosts concept
Computers or servers that attackers have successfully taken control of.
Compromised maintainer accounts technique
Compromised maintainer accounts are trusted software publisher accounts that attackers have taken over to change or release malicious code.
Compromised systems concept
Compromised systems are computers, servers, or devices that an attacker has successfully broken into or controlled.
compromised website concept
A legitimate site that has been hacked and may host malicious content or redirect visitors to phishing pages.
Compute concept
Compute means the processing power used to run software, services, or AI models.
computer fraud concept
Computer fraud is the use of computers or online systems to deceive people or commit illegal acts.
computer systems concept
Computer systems are connected hardware and software used to process information and provide digital services.
Conclave organization
A named online service or marketplace referenced in security reporting.
Conference proceedings concept
A published collection of papers presented at an academic or professional conference.
confidential information concept
Confidential information is private or sensitive data that should only be shared with authorized people.
Configuration file concept
A configuration file is a file that stores settings telling software how to run.
Connected Applications concept
Applications that have been linked to an account or service so they can access data or perform actions.
connected devices concept
Connected devices are everyday or business devices that can communicate over a network or the internet, such as phones, cameras, sensors, or appliances.
Connected-applications list concept
A wallet feature that shows external applications currently connected to the wallet.
connector tool
A connector is software that links one system or service to another so they can exchange data or actions.
conspiracy to commit access device theft concept
An agreement between people to illegally steal or misuse payment cards, account numbers, or similar access devices.
conspiracy to commit computer fraud concept
An agreement between people to carry out computer-related fraud or help others do so.
conspiracy to commit money laundering concept
Conspiracy to commit money laundering is an agreement to help hide the source of illegal money.
Contact Details concept
Information used to contact a person, such as an address, email address, or phone number.
container concept
A container is a lightweight package that runs an application with its needed files in an isolated environment.
container image scanning technique
A security practice that examines container images for vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, and malware before deployment.
container images concept
Container images are packaged snapshots of an application and its needed files that can be run consistently in container environments.
containers concept
Containers are lightweight packages that run applications with their needed files in isolated environments.
continuous concept
In security, continuous means something is monitored or updated all the time instead of only during occasional checks.
continuous monitoring concept
Continuous monitoring means constantly watching systems, accounts, or networks for problems or suspicious activity.
continuous, contextual, and automated policy enforcement concept
A security approach that automatically applies access rules continuously using the current situation and risk.
also: continuous, contextual, automated policy enforcement
Contractor concept
A person or company hired to perform work for an organization without being its regular employee.
also: the contractor, outside contractor
Contractors concept
Contractors are outside workers or companies hired to perform work for another organization.
Control plane concept
A control plane is the part of a system that manages configuration, decisions, and coordination rather than carrying user data.
coordinated vulnerability disclosure concept
A process where someone privately reports a security flaw to the maker so it can be fixed before full public details are shared.
coordination concept
Coordination is the organized sharing of tasks, information, and decisions among people or teams.
Copilot Autofix product
A GitHub Copilot feature that suggests code changes to fix security alerts.
Corelight organization
Corelight is a cybersecurity company that provides network detection and response products.
Corelight Open NDR product
A network detection and response product for monitoring and investigating network activity.
Corelight’s Open Network Detection and Response (NDR) Platform product
A Corelight security product that analyzes network activity to help detect and investigate threats.
Coruna malware
Coruna is a named malware family, cyber tool, or threat label referenced in security reporting.
CouchDB product
CouchDB is an open-source database product that stores data in flexible document-style records.
court documents other
Court documents are official records filed in a legal case.
Court Services Victoria organization
An Australian government organization that provides administrative services for courts in Victoria.
crates.io product
crates.io is the public package registry where Rust developers publish and download software libraries.
credential concept
A credential is proof of identity for logging in, such as a password, security token, API key, or certificate.
credential rotation technique
Credential rotation means replacing passwords, keys, or tokens with new ones to reduce the risk from stolen or old credentials.
credential theft technique
Credential theft is the stealing of usernames, passwords, tokens, or other login information.
credential-harvesting
Credential harvesting is collecting usernames, passwords, or login tokens from victims.
credential-stealing technique
Credential-stealing is the act of stealing login details such as passwords, session cookies, or access tokens.
credentials concept
Credentials are login details or access tokens that prove a user or system is allowed to access something.
credit-agricole other
credit-agricole is a brand-like or domain-style string that appears to reference Crédit Agricole, often relevant when checking for impersonation.
critical infrastructure concept
Critical infrastructure refers to essential systems and services that societies and organizations depend on.
Critical services concept
Critical services are essential systems or functions whose failure would seriously harm operations or public services.
Cross-border coordination concept
Cross-border coordination means organizations or law-enforcement agencies in different countries working together on the same security or crime problem.
cross-site scripting vulnerability
Cross-site scripting is a website vulnerability that lets attackers run malicious scripts in other users’ browsers.
cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability
Cross-site scripting is a web attack where malicious script runs in someone else’s browser through a trusted website.
also: XSS
crypto assets concept
Crypto assets are digital assets such as cryptocurrencies or tokens that use blockchain-related technology.
Crypto-Theft concept
Crypto-theft is the stealing of cryptocurrency, wallet keys, seed phrases, or access tokens from victims.
cryptocurrency concept
Cryptocurrency is digital money, such as Bitcoin, that uses cryptography and usually runs on a blockchain.
cryptocurrency miner tool
A cryptocurrency miner is software or hardware that performs calculations to earn cryptocurrency, sometimes installed by attackers without permission.
Cryptocurrency miners malware
Programs that use computer processing power to help create or validate cryptocurrency transactions, sometimes without the owner's permission.
cryptocurrency scam concept
A fraud scheme that uses cryptocurrency as bait or for payment, including fake investments, Ponzi schemes, and wallet drains.
cryptocurrency wallet product
A cryptocurrency wallet is software or hardware used to store and use the keys that control digital coins.
cryptocurrency wallet data concept
Information about cryptocurrency wallets, including keys, balances, and transaction history, often targeted by thieves.
Cryptocurrency wallet information concept
Cryptocurrency wallet information includes wallet addresses, keys, seed phrases, or other data used to access or track crypto funds.
Crédit Agricole organization
Crédit Agricole is a major French banking group that may be impersonated in phishing or fraud campaigns.
curl
curl is a command-line tool used to transfer data to or from servers using protocols like HTTP and HTTPS.
customer data concept
Customer data is information a company keeps about its customers, such as names, contact details, or purchase history.
customer service concept
Customer service is the support an organization provides to help users or customers solve problems.
customer services concept
Support and assistance that a company provides to its customers.
Customizable Outputs concept
Results from a tool that can be changed to include the information and format a user needs.
CVE vulnerability
A CVE is a public identifier used to track a specific known software vulnerability.
also: CVE identifier
CVEs concept
CVEs are standardized public identifiers for known cybersecurity vulnerabilities.
CVSS score concept
A CVSS score is a standard number used to show how severe a software vulnerability is.
also: CVSS score of 9.5 out of 10.0
CVSS v4 concept
CVSS v4 is version 4 of a standard scoring system used to describe how severe a security vulnerability is.
cyber concept
Cyber is a broad shorthand for things related to computers, networks, and digital security.
cyber incidents concept
Cyber incidents are events that threaten or harm computer systems, networks, or data.
cyber operations concept
Activities conducted in cyberspace including espionage, sabotage, or defense, typically by state-sponsored groups.
Cyber Partisans threat-actor
A Belarusian hacktivist group known for politically motivated cyber operations.
cyber threat concept
A cyber threat is anything that could harm computers, networks, data, or online services.
Cyber tools tool
Cyber tools are software or services used to test, monitor, defend, or attack computer systems.
cybercrime concept
Cybercrime is crime carried out using computers, networks, or the internet.
cybercriminals threat-actor
Cybercriminals are people who use computers or the internet to commit crimes such as fraud, theft, or extortion.
Cybersecurity concept
Cybersecurity is the practice of protecting computers, networks, software, and data from digital attacks or misuse.
Dark web concept
The dark web is a part of the internet that requires special tools to access and is often discussed in relation to hidden marketplaces and forums.
DarkSword malware
DarkSword is a named malware family, threat, or cyber tool referenced in security reporting.
Data access concept
Data access means the ability to view, use, change, or retrieve information from a system.
data breach concept
A data breach is an incident where sensitive, private, or protected information is accessed, exposed, or stolen without permission.
also: FBI breach, FBIjobs.gov incident
Data destruction technique
The deliberate deletion, corruption, or wiping of data so it cannot be used.
data exfiltration technique
Data exfiltration is the unauthorized removal or copying of data from a system.
data exposure concept
Data exposure means sensitive information is left accessible to people or systems that should not be able to see it.
data extortion group threat-actor
A data extortion group is a criminal group that steals or claims to steal data and demands payment to avoid leaking it.
data leak site tool
A data leak site is a website used to publish or threaten publication of stolen information.
Data sets concept
Data sets are organized collections of data used for analysis, training, reporting, or operations.
data theft concept
Data theft is the stealing of information from a system or service.
also: stole data, data-theft attacks
Dates of birth concept
Dates of birth are personal information that can help identify someone and may be sensitive if exposed.
Debug technique
Debug means to inspect software or systems to find and fix errors, and attackers can sometimes abuse debugging features to learn how something works.
debugging technique
Debugging is the process of finding and fixing problems in software code.
Decimal character-code array technique
A list of numeric character codes that must be converted back into text, often to obscure a script’s contents.
also: character-code array
Decoy Dog malware
A malware family associated with a sophisticated DNS command-and-control framework.
defaced technique
Defaced means a website has been altered without permission, often to show an attacker’s message.
default browser product
The web browser an operating system automatically uses when opening links.
defenders concept
Defenders are the people or teams responsible for protecting systems and responding to cyber threats.
Defense Department organization
The Defense Department is the U.S. government department responsible for the military and national defense.
deleted concept
Deleted means removed from normal access, though copies may sometimes still exist in backups, logs, or recovery areas.
denial-of-service
Denial-of-service is an attack that overwhelms a system so legitimate users cannot access it.
also: DoS
denial-of-service attacks technique
Denial-of-service attacks try to make a website, app, or network unavailable by overwhelming or disrupting it.
denial-of-service condition concept
A denial-of-service condition is a situation where a system becomes unavailable or unusable for legitimate users.
Dependabot tool
A GitHub tool that automatically monitors dependencies and opens pull requests to fix vulnerable packages.
dependencies concept
Dependencies are outside software components that a project relies on to work.
dependency concept
A dependency is outside software that an application relies on, which can create risk if that outside component is vulnerable or malicious.
Dependency scanning technique
Dependency scanning checks the third-party libraries an application uses to find known security flaws or risky versions.
dependency tree concept
A dependency tree is a map showing which software components depend on which others.
descriptor concept
In Tor, a descriptor is published information that tells users how to reach a hidden service.
also: signed record, public descriptor, published descriptor
Detect technique
Detect means to identify suspicious or malicious activity in systems, networks, or data.
detection concept
Detection is the process of finding signs of suspicious or malicious activity.
detection rules concept
Detection rules are instructions security tools use to flag suspicious behavior or known attack patterns.
detections concept
Alerts or findings generated by security tools indicating that a potential threat or malicious activity has been identified.
detector tool
A detector is a security rule, model, or tool that looks for signs of suspicious or malicious activity.
Detour Dog threat-actor
A threat actor or malware operation associated with using DNS infrastructure for malicious routing and distribution.
developer environments concept
Developer environments are the computers, tools, accounts, and code repositories programmers use to build software.
developer workflows concept
Developer workflows are the regular steps software developers use to write, test, review, and release code.
development forecasts concept
Predictions or plans about future development, growth, or business activity.
Device Protection product
Device Protection is a security feature or product category focused on helping protect phones, computers, or other devices from misuse or attack.
device-code vishing technique
Device-code vishing tricks people over voice calls into entering a device login code that grants attackers access.
device-code vishing attacks technique
Device-code vishing attacks use phone calls to trick victims into entering device login codes that grant attackers access.
Die Linke organization
A German democratic socialist political party.
digital estate concept
All of an organization's digital systems, accounts, applications, data, and online services considered together.
digital wallets product
Digital wallets are apps or services that store payment information, cryptocurrency keys, or other digital assets.
Digitization Trap concept
A situation where organizations apply human-focused digital processes to machine accounts even though those processes do not work well for them.
dirsearch tool
An open-source tool that looks for hidden folders and files on websites.
Disclosure concept
Disclosure is the act of reporting or publishing information about a security issue so it can be understood and fixed.
Discovery technique
Discovery is the attacker activity of learning about a victim’s systems, accounts, and network before taking further action.
disruption concept
Disruption is an interruption that prevents systems, services, or operations from working normally.
disruptive concept
Disruptive describes activity that interrupts normal use of a system, service, or business process.
distinct() technique
A data-processing operation that removes duplicate entries from a dataset.
DKIM protocol
DKIM is an email signing method that helps verify that a message was authorized by a domain and was not changed after signing.
DMARC protocol
DMARC is an email policy check that uses SPF or DKIM alignment to help determine whether a message claiming to come from a domain should be trusted.
DNS protocol
DNS is the internet system that turns human-readable names like example.com into the numeric addresses computers use to find websites and services.
also: Active DNS, DNS resolution data, DNS enumeration, dangling DNS
DNS lookups protocol
DNS lookups are requests that translate website names into the internet addresses computers use to connect.
DNS over HTTPS (DoH) protocol
A protocol that sends DNS queries through encrypted HTTPS connections.
also: DoH, public DoH services, DoH queries
DNS Record protocol
A DNS record is an entry that tells the internet how to find or handle a domain name, such as its IP address or mail server.
DNS settings concept
DNS settings control which servers a device uses to translate website names into internet addresses.
DNS TXT record protocol
A DNS TXT record is a text entry in the internet's domain-name system often used to publish verification, email security, or configuration information.
dns-hijacking technique
DNS-hijacking is an attack that changes domain-name lookups so users are sent to the wrong or malicious destination.
DNS-over-HTTPS protocol
DNS-over-HTTPS is a protocol that encrypts DNS lookups by sending them through HTTPS, making browsing requests harder to monitor or tamper with.
dns-txt-records protocol
A type of Domain Name System (DNS) record that stores text data, often used for domain ownership verification or email security policies.
also: TXT records
docker
Docker is a platform for packaging and running applications in containers.
Docker Image product
A Docker image is a packaged snapshot of an application and everything it needs to run in a container.
Dockerfile product
A Dockerfile is a text file with instructions for building a Docker image.
DockerHub product
DockerHub is an online registry where developers publish and download container images for Docker.
doj organization
DOJ usually refers to the U.S. Department of Justice, the federal agency responsible for law enforcement and legal affairs in the United States.
domain names concept
Domain names are human-readable internet addresses used to reach websites and online services.
download page concept
A download page is a web page where users can obtain software, files, or updates.
Dread product
Dread is a dark-web forum often discussed in cybercrime and underground-market reporting.
Driver concept
A driver is software that lets an operating system communicate with hardware such as a printer, graphics card, or network adapter.
also: legitimate-but-vulnerable driver
Dropbox product
Dropbox is a cloud storage and file-sharing service.
dropper malware
A dropper is malware whose main job is to install or unpack other malware onto a device.
DS-Fusion malware
A malware package referenced in security reporting that combines DarkSword and Coruna components.
DTLS protocol
DTLS is a security protocol that protects datagram network traffic, similar to how TLS protects web connections.
DTLS Analyzer tool
A network-analysis component that recognizes and records information about DTLS-encrypted traffic.
also: existing DTLS analyzer
Dutch National Police organization
The Dutch National Police is the national police force of the Netherlands.
Dynamic testing technique
Dynamic testing checks software while it is running to see how it behaves and whether vulnerabilities appear.
E-ZPass product
An electronic toll-collection system used on roads and bridges in parts of the United States.
EBurst tool
EBurst is a password-guessing tool that can attempt many login credentials against Microsoft Exchange servers.
EC2 product
Amazon EC2 is Amazon Web Services’ cloud service for renting virtual servers.
Ed25519 protocol
Ed25519 is a modern digital-signature algorithm used to prove data or messages came from the expected sender and were not changed.
Edge product
Edge is Microsoft’s web browser, officially called Microsoft Edge.
also: edge address, edge addresses
edge.exe tool
A filename resembling the Microsoft Edge browser that attackers may use to disguise malicious software.
Email security concept
Email security protects inboxes and users from threats such as phishing, malware, and scam messages.
employee data concept
Employee data is information an organization keeps about its workers, such as names, contact details, job records, or payroll information.
employment information concept
Employment information is personal data about someone's job, workplace, role, or work history.
Enablement package product
A small Windows update that turns on features already included in an earlier version.
encrypted concept
Encrypted data has been scrambled so that only someone with the right key can read it.
EndGame tool
A toolkit referenced in security reporting that helps websites resist denial-of-service attacks.
Endor Labs organization
Endor Labs is a cybersecurity company focused on software supply chain security.
Endorsement requirements concept
Rules requiring a new author to be approved or supported before they can submit work.
endpoint concept
An endpoint is a user device such as a laptop, phone, or server that connects to a network.
Endpoint enforcement concept
Security controls applied directly to computers or devices to restrict what software can do.
endpoints concept
Endpoints are user-facing devices such as laptops, desktops, or phones that connect to systems and data.
Enterprise networks concept
Enterprise networks are the large computer networks used by businesses, governments, or other organizations.
enumerate technique
To enumerate means to systematically list or discover items such as users, devices, services, or files during security testing.
ESC1 technique
ESC1 is a known Active Directory Certificate Services misconfiguration pattern that can let attackers request certificates useful for impersonation.
also: ADCS ESC1 misconfigurations
Essential Services concept
Services people depend on for daily life and public safety, such as power, water, healthcare, and government services.
Ethereal Panda threat-actor
Ethereal Panda is a threat-actor tracking name used by security researchers for related malicious activity.
Europol organization
Europol is the European Union’s law enforcement agency that helps member countries fight serious and organized crime.
evade detection technique
To evade detection means to hide malicious activity so security tools or analysts do not notice it.
Event types concept
Event types are categories used to label different kinds of recorded system activity.
excessive access concept
Excessive access means a person or account has more permissions than they actually need, increasing security risk.
executable concept

exploitation technique

extradited concept

fake companies concept
